keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review repair 2026-10-19). The shape is unchanged; the status is not: the Makk is "restored as a British client state" (lead) and "remained closely controlled by the British", and "The Makks of Taqali proved to be useful allies and the British gradually gave them more territory to control and administer" (no extent given), "through to the independence of Sudan in 1956"; administrative power ended with the 1969 coup. The vassal events in the ledger carry this, so the same land is drawn as the vassal tint of British Africa and then of the Republic of Sudan, not as a sovereign state. No area figure on the page.

ledger.note: c. 1750: Muhammad wad Jayli founds the Kingdom of Taqali in the Nuba Mountains. Infobox "1750" as the start; the page says it "is believed to have been founded in the eighteenth century", some scholars 1750-1780, oral tradition the early sixteenth century.

region.text: all of the Nuba Mountains, centred on the Taqali Massif

ledger.note: 1821 onward: Taqali pays a nominal tax to Egypt. "Sennar adhered to this arrangement until the Egyptian invasion of Sennar in 1821." "The Egyptians then launched three failed invasions against Taqali." "An agreement was reached with Egypt that Taqali would remain de facto independent", would "pay a nominal tax and be officially incorporated into Egyptian Sudan." The page dates neither the invasions nor the agreement; 1821, the last dated event before them, is a bridge, and the agreement may be later (no reign is named). Nominal tribute and official incorporation, drawn as the lightest vassal tint of the Egyptian Sudan.

ledger.note: July 1884: the Egyptian tribute ends with the Mahdist conquest. "In July 1884 the ruler of Taqali, Makk Adam, was captured by the Mahdists"; the page does not say when Egyptian suzerainty lapsed, so the month of the capture is used as a bridge.

region.text: all of the Nuba Mountains, centred on the Taqali Massif

ledger.note: July 1884: the Mahdists take the kingdom. "In July 1884 the ruler of Taqali, Makk Adam, was captured by the Mahdists"; the lead says Taqali was "conquered by Sudanese Mahdists in 1884" and the body "by the forces of the self-proclaimed Mahdi" in the 'late 19th century'; rulers table: "Interregnum 1884-1898". Year 1884 is the page's; the extent of the Mahdist hold over all the Nuba Mountains is the page's description of the state. The Mahdist State page, read 2026-10-19, never mentions Taqali or the Nuba Mountains; the matching Mahdist gain (mahdist-state /ledger/3, July 1884) was added by fix fx-16 on 2026-11-01 from this page.

region.text: all of the Nuba Mountains, centred on the Taqali Massif

ledger.note: 1898: the Makk is restored by the British. Rulers table: Jayli from 1898, "Interregnum 1884-1898"; the Mahdist State page, read 2026-10-19, has the Mahdist State "terminated by Anglo-Egyptian forces in 1898" (Omdurman, 2 September 1898). The Taqali page's own text says "In 1889 the Mahdists were defeated by the British, who formed Anglo-Egyptian Sudan" and the lead "restored as a British client state" in 1889, which conflicts with its table and with the Mahdist State page; 1898 is used. Counterpart changed from british-africa to mahdist-state by fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): the Mahdist State holds the Nuba Mountains from July 1884 (mahdist-state /ledger/3) and loses them in 1898 (mahdist-state /ledger/17), so the gain has to come from it for the compiler to move the cells; the page names the British as the power that restored the Makk, and that relation is the vassal_start that follows. The Mahdist hold ended with the British victory over the Khalifa (Mahdist State page).

wars.name: Egyptian invasions of Taqali
wars.outcome: "The Egyptians then launched three failed invasions against Taqali"; Taqali stayed de facto independent paying a nominal tax and was officially incorporated into Egyptian Sudan.
wars.note: The page gives no years for the three invasions; 1821-1840 brackets the reigns it places them in. Before 1821 Sennar "was appeased by annual payments from Taqali" (the Funj dossier's vassal_start for the Taqali dates 1665). Review repair: the page gives only the 1821 invasion of Sennar and no date for the three Taqali invasions or the agreement; 1821-1840 is a bridge, and the tribute relation is recorded as a vassal_start of turco-egyptian-sudan in the ledger (confidence 1).

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria lacks Taqali. One page opened (Kingdom of Taqali; budget 1-2). Disagreements: the funj-sultanate dossier (af-01-b) has a vassal_start for 'kingdom-of-taqali' in 1665 (confidence 1, from the Funj page) while this page dates the state to the 18th century (infobox 1750, tradition early 16th century) and says Sennar 'was appeased by annual payments from Taqali' without using the word vassal; the British 'defeated the Mahdists in 1889' (page) against the rulers table's Jayli from 1898. After 1898 the Makk was a 'controlled ally' of the British (the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan dossier should treat the Nuba Mountains as British; this dossier keeps the infobox end of 1969, a ceremonial role afterwards). Mahdist State is the counterpart for 1884; the Mahdist dossier of af-01-c has no Taqali event. Gazetteer: Abbasiyya (capital) approximate coordinate.
Review repair (2026-10-19): the single keyframe is split at the Mahdist interregnum (1750-1883, then 1898-1969); the Egyptian nominal-tax relation (vassal of turco-egyptian-sudan from 1821, confidence 1, undated on the page), the British client relation (1898-1956, british-africa) and the 1956-1969 relation to the Republic of Sudan (a reading) are recorded as vassal events instead of a sovereign state; the 1898 regain now names british-africa. The Mahdist conquest is dated 1884 by the Taqali page's own lead (July 1884 capture of the Makk); the Mahdist State page is silent on Taqali. Not settled: the 1889 (text, lead) against 1898 (rulers table, Mahdist State page) date of the restoration; the year of the Egyptian agreement; whether Taqali was a vassal of the Republic of Sudan at all after 1956. For af-01-c: the mahdist-state dossier has no gain of the Nuba Mountains in 1884 and no loss in 1898; for af-08: british-africa and republic-of-sudan could carry the mirror vassal_start events.
Fix fx-16 (2026-11-01): the Mahdist dossier now carries the matching events (mahdist-state /ledger/3 gain, July 1884; /ledger/17 loss, 1898) and no longer draws the Nuba Mountains in its 1881, 1883, 1898 and 1899 keyframes, so the conflicts of those years are gone; /ledger/4 now names mahdist-state as counterpart. kingdom-of-taqali_1750 keeps its end year 1883: a keyframe only sets the state in its first year, the ledger holds the kingdom through 1884 until the July loss, and the pages describe no contested phase before the capture. The Egyptian relation (/ledger/1) is a vassal_start on the Turco-Egyptian Sudan; data/hierarchy.csv already draws the Taqali inside the Khedivate of Egypt 1866-1883.
